claim_text: IDScan.net 0.53% → 2.15% fraud rate trajectory over two years, 1M+ transaction dataset

primary_source_confirmed.title: Surging ID fraud in US cargo and logistics, report finds — IDScan.net 2026 Cargo and Logistics ID Fraud Report
primary_source_confirmed.dataset_size: More than 1 million identity verification transactions
primary_source_confirmed.sector_coverage: Processing, manufacturing, transport, and warehousing operations (US)
primary_source_confirmed.trajectory_note: 213% increase over two years; Q2 2025 was highest quarterly rate on record, running 75% above historical average
primary_source_confirmed.notes: Vendor-produced report from IDScan.net's own platform transaction data. No independent verification. IDScan.net processes 21M+ verifications/month across 20,000+ global locations.

corroborating_sources.title: Identity fraud attempts in logistics sector rise 4x over two years — DC Velocity
corroborating_sources.key_data: Relays identical IDScan.net figures (0.53% → 1.66% → 2.15%), no independent data added

corroborating_sources.title: 2025 ID Fraud Report: Business risk skyrockets as ID fraud rises — IDScan.net
corroborating_sources.key_data: Cross-sector report confirming cargo/logistics 61.4% increase in Q4 2024; does NOT supply an overall fraud rate percentage for logistics
corroborating_sources.notes: Same vendor, different report. Confirms directional trend but uses breakdown-by-detection-method rather than overall fraud rate %.

corroborating_sources.title: TIA State of Fraud in the Industry — April 2025 Report
corroborating_sources.key_data: 1,600+ fraud reports filed on TIA Watchdog (Sep 2024–Feb 2025), 65% increase from prior period; 83% of respondents experienced 3+ fraud types in 6 months; 97% cite truckload as most fraud-prone mode
corroborating_sources.independent_corroboration: partial — confirms strong upward trajectory but uses report-count and survey-% metrics, not transaction-level fraud rates
corroborating_sources.limitations: Survey sample size (N) not disclosed publicly; no per-100-loads incidence rate

corroborating_sources.title: Truckstop 2025 Freight Fraud Report: What 63,000 Fraud Checks Reveal About Prevention
corroborating_sources.key_data_from_search: 63,000 entities reviewed; 12,768 suspicious RMIS onboarding attempts blocked; 9,984 suspicious load board access attempts blocked in 2024; does NOT express as % of total transactions
corroborating_sources.independent_corroboration: partial — confirms large-scale booking-layer fraud volume but no comparable transaction-rate metric

corroborating_sources.title: Highway Q1 2025 Freight Fraud Index
corroborating_sources.fetch_status: Landing page only — full data behind download gate
corroborating_sources.key_data_from_search: 400,000 sophisticated fraud attempts in Q1 2025; 352,134 fraudulent inbound emails; 406 unauthorized FMCSA contact changes; 30,921 fraudulent/spoofed calls. Q1 2026: 527,940 blocked email threats, 169.6% YoY surge in ownership-change fraud
corroborating_sources.independent_corroboration: directional — confirms accelerating identity/impersonation fraud at booking layer, but metric is absolute count not transaction rate

claim_correction_note: The original claim states '0.53% → 2.15% over two years.' This is accurate directionally but omits the intermediate 2024 datapoint of 1.66%. The full trajectory is 0.53% (2023) → 1.66% (2024) → 2.15% (2025). Consider updating claim to reflect three-year progression.
suggested_revision: IDScan.net's 2026 Cargo and Logistics ID Fraud Report — drawing on 1M+ identity verification transactions across US transport and warehousing — found identity fraud attempt rates rose from 0.53% (2023) to 1.66% (2024) to 2.15% (2025), a 4x increase over two years [IDScan.net primary, vendor-produced]. TIA Watchdog (April 2025) independently corroborates accelerating trajectory with a 65% jump in fraud reports over the prior six-month period [industry-association, partial corroboration].
score_rationale: Primary IDScan.net URL confirmed with exact figures (0.53%/1.66%/2.15%, 1M+ dataset). However the dataset is vendor-proprietary with no independent audit or disclosed methodology. No second source publishes a comparable transaction-rate metric. TIA and Highway data corroborate the trend direction but use incommensurable metrics (report counts, blocked emails). Score upgrades from Low to Medium: primary source confirmed but remains single-vendor, unaudited.
